record.population: 574 African schoolgirls (6-21 years) and 604 women (18-86 years), South Africa
record.design: Two population studies analysed together; clinical assessment of traction alopecia (TA) with a severity score; logistic regression
record.finding: TA was present in 17.1% of schoolgirls and 31.7% of women. Risk was highest when traction was added to relaxed hair (odds ratio 3.47 against natural hair, 95% CI 1.94-6.20). Odds were higher with braiding-related than chemical-related symptoms. Only 18.9% of people with TA had never had hairdressing-related symptoms.
record.note: Cross-sectional, so it shows association not cause; the authors suggest avoiding hairdressing symptoms and added traction, especially on chemically processed hair.
